intro: Hello! In this lesson you'll learn the simple present — the tense for habits, routines and facts, like 'I work in an office' or 'She drinks coffee every morning'. The tricky part is the -s for he/she/it, and using do/does for questions and negatives. Warm-up: what do you do every morning?
teachingNotes: Indonesian verbs don't change, so third-person -s is the #1 error (*'She work').
Negatives: don't + base verb (I/you/we/they), doesn't + base verb (he/she/it). Never *'doesn't works'.
Questions: Do/Does + subject + base verb. Short answers: Yes, I do / No, she doesn't.
Spelling: go → goes, watch → watches, study → studies, have → has.
Tie practice to daily routines: get up, have breakfast, go to work, start, finish.

keyPoints.title: Affirmative and the he/she/it -s
keyPoints.explanation: Use the base verb with I, you, we, they. Add -s or -es with he, she, it: I work → she works, I go → he goes.

examples.en: My father works in a bank.

keyPoints.title: Negatives with don't / doesn't
keyPoints.explanation: don't + base verb for I/you/we/they; doesn't + base verb for he/she/it. The -s moves to 'does', so the main verb has no -s.

keyPoints.title: Questions with do / does
keyPoints.explanation: Do/Does + subject + base verb: Do you play football? Does he live here? Answer: Yes, I do. / No, he doesn't.

examples.en: Do you speak English? — Yes, I do.
What time does she start work?

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with 'work': She ___ in a hospital.
Make it negative: He plays tennis.
Make a question: You like music.

independentPractice.prompt: Write one sentence about what time you get up.
Make a question about Rina: (live) in Surabaya?

assessment.prompt: Complete with 'go': My brother ___ to school by bus.
Make it negative: We eat meat.
Make it negative: She watches TV.
assessment.rubric: Correct: She doesn't watch TV. 'doesn't watches' = 50.

assessment.prompt: Make a question: He speaks Japanese.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Does he speak Japanese? 'Does he speaks' = 50.

assessment.prompt: Write one sentence about what you do in the evening (use the simple present).
assessment.rubric: Any correct simple present sentence about an evening routine scores 100. Third-person or tense errors reduce the score.

blocks.text: Use the simple present for **habits**, **routines** and **facts**: things that are generally true, not just right now. Time words like *every day*, *usually* and *on Mondays* are a good sign.

id.text: Simple present dipakai untuk **kebiasaan**, **rutinitas** dan **fakta**: hal yang umumnya benar, bukan hanya saat ini. Kata waktu seperti *every day*, *usually* dan *on Mondays* adalah tandanya.

rows.en: We go to the gym on Mondays.

blocks.text: With I, you, we and they, use the base verb. With **he, she, it** (one person or thing), add **-s**: *she works*. Add **-es** after s, sh, ch, x and o: *he watches, she goes*. Consonant + y → **-ies**: *study → studies*.

id.text: Dengan I, you, we dan they, pakai kata kerja dasar. Dengan **he, she, it** (satu orang atau benda), tambahkan **-s**: *she works*. Tambahkan **-es** setelah s, sh, ch, x dan o: *he watches, she goes*. Konsonan + y → **-ies**: *study → studies*.

rows.en: My father works in a bank.
She goes to school by bus.

blocks.explain: Watch ends in ch, so he/she adds -es: watches.

id.explain: Watch berakhiran ch, jadi untuk he/she ditambah -es: watches.

blocks.text: Use **don't** + base verb with I/you/we/they and **doesn't** + base verb with he/she/it. The -s moves to *does*, so the main verb has **no -s**: *She doesn't like rain*.

id.text: Pakai **don't** + kata kerja dasar untuk I/you/we/they dan **doesn't** + kata kerja dasar untuk he/she/it. Huruf -s pindah ke *does*, jadi kata kerja utama **tanpa -s**: *She doesn't like rain*.

blocks.explain: He → doesn't, and the verb stays in the base form: eat.

id.explain: He → doesn't, dan kata kerjanya tetap bentuk dasar: eat.

blocks.text: Start with **Do** or **Does**, then the subject, then the base verb: *Do you speak English? Does he live here?* Short answers: **Yes, I do. / No, he doesn't.**

id.text: Mulai dengan **Do** atau **Does**, lalu subjek, lalu kata kerja dasar: *Do you speak English? Does he live here?* Jawaban singkat: **Yes, I do. / No, he doesn't.**

rows.en: Do you speak English? — Yes, I do.
rows.id: Apakah kamu bisa berbahasa Inggris? — Ya.

rows.en: What time does she start work?

blocks.text: Talking about your routine is one of the first real conversations you'll have: *I start work at nine. I usually have lunch at twelve. In the evening I cook and watch TV.* It's also the tense of instructions and documentation: *The app saves your work automatically.*

id.text: Menceritakan rutinitas adalah salah satu percakapan nyata pertama yang akan kamu alami: *I start work at nine. I usually have lunch at twelve. In the evening I cook and watch TV.* Ini juga tense untuk instruksi dan dokumentasi: *The app saves your work automatically.*

blocks.text: Most mistakes are the missing -s with he/she/it. Check every he/she/it sentence once.

id.text: Kesalahan paling sering adalah lupa -s untuk he/she/it. Periksa setiap kalimat he/she/it sekali lagi.

suggestedQuestions: Why do we add -s with he/she/it?
Why is it 'doesn't like', not 'doesn't likes'?
How is this different from am/is/are?

id.intro: Halo! Di pelajaran ini kamu akan belajar simple present — tense untuk kebiasaan, rutinitas dan fakta, seperti 'I work in an office' atau 'She drinks coffee every morning'. Bagian yang menantang adalah tambahan -s untuk he/she/it, serta do/does untuk pertanyaan dan kalimat negatif. Pemanasan: apa yang kamu lakukan setiap pagi?
